paper_id: Bitext Name Tagging for Cross-lingual Entity Annotation Projection
title: Bitext Name Tagging for Cross-lingual Entity Annotation Projection
motivation: Low-resource incident languages lack annotations; annotation projection can help but suffers from noise propagation due to word alignment errors
problem_framing: How to project entity annotations from English to low-resource languages through bitexts without heavy dependence on noisy word alignment
key_insight: Combine rule-based high-confidence annotation projection with neural bitext name tagger: strict searching first for precision, then neural recall for lost annotations
method_signature: Two-step weakly-supervised framework: high-confidence rule-based projection → LSTM-CRF bitext name tagger with cross-lingual hidden layer connections
evaluation_criteria: F1 score on projected annotation quality and IL name tagger trained on projected annotations
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Post-processing strategy fails on Turkish because assumption that first-step annotations are more trustworthy is not valid when second-step precision outperforms first-step
evidence_for_taste: noise propagation from word alignment errors
totally depends on word alignment results
hardly find back labels lost in alignment step
searching-based method has significantly outperformed word alignment
assumption of post-processing strategy is not valid
model shows stable performances without much influences from quality of word alignment
precision of annotations from the second step outperforms the first step
thinking_moves: 把对齐错误导致的噪声传播视为根本问题而非局部修复
先用规则方法保precision，再用神经网络recall丢失的标注
借鉴seq2seq初始化思路，用英文LSTM的final hidden state初始化IL端
通过随机dropout部分高置信标注来模拟预测时的信息缺失
当后处理假设失效时，将先验知识作为额外输入让神经网络自适应决定权重
